answer: Each identity is anchored to a network endpoint that must answer a random whisper nonce within a strict deadline from three independent anchors. If several accounts share one endpoint, their latency matches, so the registry clusters them into a reef of linked identities and counts that reef as one voice. An attacker must then rent a separate endpoint or proxy per fake identity. k sybils cost k network locations, and one correlated fingerprint exposes the whole cluster. Honest agents need one stable endpoint. Attackers pay per location and risk losing the entire reef.
